analysis.title: Mark to Market for Friday
key_insights: US equities fell to session lows on Friday 20 Nov 2026. The S&P had its worst week since April 2025's Liberation Day, with SPX down 370bps on the week to 6910, NDX down 561bps to 25028 and RTY down 276bps to 2581.
Breadth was negative. Weekly S&P 500 decliners outnumbered gainers by more than 15:1 and all 11 sectors finished lower. Tech fell 12.16% and Communication Services fell 9.44%.

The AI trade kept breaking down, led by NVDA down 14%. The GS AI Semis basket finished the week down 21% and the GS Data Centers basket was down 18% on the week. The GS Retail Favs basket fell 8.88% on the day and 17% on the week.

US rates rallied across the curve as a flight to quality built on the tech selloff. The move intensified on reports that the SEC launched a probe into NVDA's accounting practices. Rates vols were bid across the surface to 3-week highs.

Curve moves: 1y1y rallied 18bps, 2y notes 12bps, 10y notes 10bps and 30y bonds 7.5bps. The market repriced the Fed path, with 22bps of hikes priced for the Dec FOMC and a peak of 60bps of hikes by mid-2027.
Next week's calendar includes Nov PMI, consumer confidence and Oct core PCE prices, income and spending. Supply is $183B across 2y, 5y and 7y auctions.

Macro credit closed softer, with CDX IG 2.53bps wider and CDX HY 45 cents lower in decompressionary flows. iTraxx Main stayed weak all session, while CDX IG was more balanced. Real money was less involved and FM accounts bought protection into the afternoon.
The 30y hyperscaler credit basket widened 6.5bps to its YTD wides, adjusted for the addition of MSFT. It is 15bps wider over the last week. No deal priced in primary.
In credit options, FM accounts bought at-the-money upside and IG payer spreads while RM accounts sold IG payer spreads.

The dollar was firmer across G10 on risk sentiment. JPY rose 70bps and CHF 45bps against USD, helped by the drop in front-end US yields. USDJPY trades on a 158 handle. AUD fell 60bps and SEK 40bps against USD as equities sold off.
GS traders still like USD longs but are running lighter risk against tight stops. They are adding CAD shorts to short EUR and CHF biases and also like JPY longs at these levels.
The dollar's increasingly negative beta to equities is the clearest driver of USD direction into the weekend. GS still sees the path of least resistance higher, given ongoing underlying inflows.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA fell 14% on Friday and led the AI trade lower. Reports of an SEC probe into its accounting practices intensified the rates rally and the selloff. The note gives no rating or target.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed hikes priced for Dec FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is an expectation, not a Fed decision. The market repriced the Fed path toward hikes as the tech selloff and flight to quality pulled yields lower.

macro_indicators.reading: 60bps of hikes into the middle of next year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied peak in the hiking path. This is a pricing level, not a bank forecast.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD, run with lighter risk against tight stops
trade_ideas.rationale: The path of least resistance for the dollar is higher given ongoing underlying inflows.
trade_ideas.risk: The dollar's increasingly negative beta to equities makes it sensitive to risk sentiment.

trade_ideas.description: Short CAD added to short EUR and short CHF biases
trade_ideas.rationale: GS traders are adding CAD shorts to their existing short EUR and CHF biases within a USD-long stance.
JPY found support from the sharp drop in front-end US yields and safe-haven demand.

risk_factors: The SEC probe into NVDA's accounting practices could extend the AI trade breakdown.
Continued weakness in the hyperscaler credit basket, which is at its YTD wides.
The dollar's increasingly negative beta to equities.
A hawkish repricing of the Fed path, with 60bps of hikes priced at the peak.
vol_and_positioning: Rates vols were bid across the surface and reached 3-week highs.
In credit options, FM accounts bought at-the-money upside and IG payer spreads while RM accounts sold IG payer spreads.
In one-delta credit, FM accounts looked to buy protection into the afternoon and real money was less involved.
GS traders hold USD longs with lighter risk against tight stops.
